key_insight: An exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion model shows that CT-CS energy alignment is the main knob controlling the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaics.
engineering_relevance: The model gives device designers practical rules for tuning singlet/triplet energetics and triplet recycling to improve photocurrent while limiting voltage penalties.
method: Self-consistent exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion simulation of charge transport and excited-state populations
Includes reversible singlet/triplet transitions with LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T offsets
Analyzes transient and steady-state behavior to separate generation, recombination, extraction, and voltage-loss effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends.
watch_item: The recommended CT-CS and CT-T alignments may be highly sensitive to temperature and material-specific energetics, so experimental calibration is needed before transfer to new blends.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
